subject.title: I updated Scrapling and the skill became hidden again

question: Should confirmed recurring Scrapling false positives receive a narrowly scoped clearance mechanism across updates, or must every new version remain hidden until an independent scan or human review clears it?
rationale: The decision trades publisher continuity against the requirement that changed release contents receive fresh security evaluation; source inspection cannot safely choose that trust policy.

options.title: Keep per-version review
options.body: Continue scanning every release, but add clear owner diagnostics, an in-product Fix/Appeal action, and timely review escalation for repeated false positives.

options.title: Carry forward clearance
options.body: Persist approval for this publisher or skill lineage across updates, accepting the risk that changed files could inherit trust before review.

options.title: Retain manual unlocks
options.body: Keep the current support-mediated process, preserving the strictest boundary but continuing the recurring release blocker.

recommendation.title: Keep per-version review
recommendation.body: Continue scanning every release, but add clear owner diagnostics, an in-product Fix/Appeal action, and timely review escalation for repeated false positives.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the active RFC covering hidden listings, human review, and scanner-based enforcement categories.
